name: ASM Technologies Ltd
tagline: Engineering-R&D-services firm mid-inflection into Design-Led Manufacturing of semiconductor/solar/aerospace capital equipment (DLM now 73.6% of revenue, Q1 FY27 revenue +62% YoY, EBITDA margin ~23%, CFO turned positive) with a credible ECMS policy catalyst and a new 50:50 ASM-HHV semiconductor-equipment JV -- but the stock trades at ~127x earnings / ~30x book after a ~100x re-rating from 2020 lows, new-plant asset turns are unproven, and MD's-sons remuneration is a governance watch-item.
business_overview: Two segments: HiTech (design, prototyping, qualification and manufacturing of semiconductor/industrial capital equipment — the growth engine, via ASM Technologies / HHV – Hind High Vacuum) and Engineering Services (Forms & Gears precision mechanicals, product engineering for aerospace/industrial clients). Minority stakes / acquisitions: Myelin Foundry (20%, edge AI), Asmaitha Wireless (electronics/control). New plants at Dabaspet and Sriperumbudur operational; Rs 250 Cr Hosur LED-equipment facility; among the first firms to receive Capital-Goods-category grants under the government's ECMS with a ~Rs 565 Cr capex plan.

~127x / ~30x -- ~100x re-rated from 2020 lows; no margin of safety

fundamentals_narrative: The revenue inflection is real and cash-backed: consolidated revenue Rs 202 Cr (FY24) -> Rs 289 Cr -> Rs 529 Cr (FY26), quarterly revenue Rs 115 Cr (Q1 FY26) -> Rs 199 Cr (Q1 FY27, +62% YoY), EBITDA margin expanded from ~3% (FY24) to ~23% (Q1 FY27), and operating cash flow turned positive (Rs 68 Cr FY26) after two negative years. Design-Led Manufacturing -- design, prototyping, qualification and manufacturing of semiconductor/solar/aerospace capital equipment -- is now 73.6% of revenue and is the engine; the positioning is reinforced by a 50:50 ASM-HHV JV (vacuum/thin-film tools) and by ASM being an early ECMS Capital-Goods grantee with a ~Rs 565 Cr capex plan (new plants at Dabaspet and Sriperumbudur operational, a Rs 250 Cr Hosur LED-equipment facility). ROCE is ~27%. Against all that: the stock trades at ~127x earnings and ~30x book after re-rating roughly 100x from its 2020 lows (and 2-4x in the last year); the ramp is on a small base with lumpy project revenue; Q3 FY26 disappointed even long-term bulls; new-plant asset turns are unproven while a large capex phase runs (so free cash flow is negative despite positive CFO); and there are governance watch-items -- the MD's sons draw remuneration high relative to their roles (one, an 'Executive Director' who is also a professional racing driver, paid ~Rs 2.97 Cr in FY26, more than the MD), plus flagged new-ERP and overseas-subsidiary execution problems.
